newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - up 1/8 in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - up 1/8 in quiet trade.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were up about 1/8 in a quiet cash market Thursday, but traders are hoping for more energetic activity.
On Wednesday, municipals regained some lost ground late in the day, but ended the day in the loss column, off 1/8.
For Thursday so far, the market is up marginally -- cash is not up as much as futures, traders said.
"The tone is okay," said one trader. "We are fearful that there will not be a lot of trading. There are no new issues to really focus on today. I'm afraid it will be a lackluster, moderate day."
"Everyone will be trying generate some interest," the trader said. "It is a market that needs to be prodded into trading."
Another trader said that there were a "couple of bid lists from customers" but not a lot of activity.
And the "numbers looked okay for the market," he added.

The Commerce Department said the February trade gap was $11.59 billion. Wall Street economnists had forecast a February trade deficit of $10.1 billion. The U.S. Department of Labor said initial state jobless benefit claims, seasonally adjusted, rose to 332,000 the week ended April12 from revised 324,000 prior week. Wall Street econiomists had forecast initial jobless claims of 317,000 in the April 12 week.
The 30-year U.S Treasury bond was up 6/32 to yield 7.08 percent.
In primary market action for Thursday, municipal bond sales are expected to total $169 million in 17 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings total $143 million in five sales, with a $97 million Missouri Housing Development Corporation through A.G. Edwards & Sons, Inc. topping the list.
On the competitive side, 12 sales totaling $26 million are on the schedule. A $23 million Sarrah Scott Middle School District, Ind., deal at 1400 EDT is the largest.
An additional nine sales totaling $256 million are on the possible calender, meaning underwriters have said they may price the bonds Thursday, depending on market conditions.
In secondary market activity, Delaware River Port FGIC-insured 5-1/2s due 2001 were quoted at a 5.86 bid, 5.80 offered. On Wednesday, the bonds were quoted with a 5.85 bid and 5.82 offered.

In debt futures, June Treasury bonds were up eight ticks to 107-23/32, while June municipal bonds were up eight ticks to 112-17/32. The MOB spread was 159, wider than its close at 154 ticks on Wednesday.
